newsitem.title: CHINA: Visitor arrivals to Hong Kong down 14 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: Visitor arrivals to Hong Kong down 14 pct in June.

text.p: Visitor arrivals to Hong Kong fell 14.1 percent year-on-year to just over 789,000 in June, the Hong Kong Tourist Association said on Monday.

The association said in a statement the number was smaller than expected, attributing the fall to misconcpetions about the availability of hotel rooms in the run-up to China's recovery of Hong Kong June 30.

"Despite our best efforts to assure the world that we had rooms available, many people just presumed we would be flooded with visitors in the lead-up to such an historic event," the association's executive director Amy Chan said in the statement.
Chan said the July figure was also likely to fall on last year, but noted the period from June to August was traditionally an off-season.

"However, this year the quieter period has been compounded by an inevitable lull after the huge build-up to the change of sovereignty, as many markets take a wait-and-see attitude," Chan said. "We had fully anticipated this."
But she expected the World Bank/International Monetary Fund (IMF) meetings due to take place in Hong Kong in September to bring visitors to the territory.
"We can also look forward to the World Bank/IMF meetings in September which will once again put the international spotlight on Hong Kong," she said.
Visitor arrivals grew 5.2 percent to 5.7 million in the first half of this year, compared with the growth rate of 9.2 percent for the first five months of 1997.

The Hong Kong government has said it expects over 12 million tourists this year, spending US$12.27 billion. A total of 11.7 million visitors arrived last year, spending about HK$82.46 billion (US$10.65 billion).
